title: 204. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Absolute Value Inequalities
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Solving basic absolute value inequalities of the form \(|x|<a\)
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|x|<a\) and express the solution as a compound inequality.
questions.question: Solve \(|x|<4\).
questions.explanation: The inequality \(|x|<4\) means that the distance from \(x\) to \(0\) is less than \(4\). Therefore \(x\) must lie between \(-4\) and \(4\), so the solution is \(-4<x<4\). The option \(x<-4\) or \(x>4\) describes \(|x|>4\), not \(|x|<4\).
questions.hint: Recall that \(|x|<a\) means the distance from \(x\) to \(0\) is less than \(a\).

questions.concept: Solving basic absolute value inequalities of the form \(|x|>a\)
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|x|>a\) and express the solution as a union of two intervals.
questions.question: Solve \(|x|>3\).
questions.explanation: The inequality \(|x|>3\) means that the distance from \(x\) to \(0\) is greater than \(3\). Thus \(x\) must be less than \(-3\) or greater than \(3\). The solution is \(x<-3\) or \(x>3\). The option \(-3<x<3\) describes \(|x|<3\), not \(|x|>3\).
questions.hint: For \(|x|>a\), split the inequality into \(x<-a\) or \(x>a\).

questions.concept: Solving absolute value inequalities with a shifted expression
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|x-a|\le b\) by rewriting it as a compound inequality.
questions.question: Solve \(|x-2|\le 5\).
questions.explanation: Rewrite \(|x-2|\le 5\) as \(-5\le x-2\le 5\). Add \(2\) to all parts: \(-3\le x\le 7\). Therefore the solution is \(-3\le x\le 7\). The option \(x\le -3\) or \(x\ge 7\) is the solution of \(|x-2|\ge 5\), not \(|x-2|\le 5\).
questions.hint: An inequality of the form \(|u|\le b\) becomes \(-b\le u\le b\).

questions.concept: Solving absolute value inequalities with a linear expression
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|ax+b|\ge c\) by splitting into two linear inequalities.
questions.question: Solve \(|2x+1|\ge 5\).
questions.explanation: The inequality \(|2x+1|\ge 5\) means \(2x+1\ge 5\) or \(2x+1\le -5\). First, \(2x+1\ge 5\) gives \(2x\ge 4\), so \(x\ge 2\). Second, \(2x+1\le -5\) gives \(2x\le -6\), so \(x\le -3\). Therefore the solution is \(x\le -3\) or \(x\ge 2\). The option \(-3\le x\le 2\) is the solution of \(|2x+1|\le 5\), not \(|2x+1|\ge 5\).

questions.concept: Solving strict absolute value inequalities with a linear expression
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|ax+b|<c\) by forming a compound inequality.
questions.question: Solve \(|3x-4|<2\).
questions.explanation: Rewrite \(|3x-4|<2\) as \(-2<3x-4<2\). Add \(4\) to all parts: \(2<3x<6\). Divide by \(3\): \(\frac{2}{3}<x<2\). Therefore the solution is \(\frac{2}{3}<x<2\). The option \(x<\frac{2}{3}\) or \(x>2\) corresponds to \(|3x-4|>2\), not \(|3x-4|<2\).

questions.concept: Isolating the absolute value before solving an inequality
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute value inequality after first isolating the absolute value expression.
questions.question: Solve \(|x+3|+2\le 5\).
questions.explanation: Subtract \(2\) from both sides to isolate the absolute value: \(|x+3|\le 3\). Then rewrite as \(-3\le x+3\le 3\). Subtract \(3\) from all parts: \(-6\le x\le 0\). Therefore the solution is \(-6\le x\le 0\). The option \(x\le -6\) or \(x\ge 0\) would arise from treating the inequality as \(|x+3|\ge 3\).
questions.hint: First isolate the absolute value expression, then rewrite it as a compound inequality.

questions.concept: Solving strict absolute value inequalities with a linear expression
questions.learningObjective: Solve \(|ax+b|>c\) by writing the solution as a union of intervals.
questions.question: Solve \(|2x-1|>7\).
questions.explanation: The inequality \(|2x-1|>7\) means \(2x-1>7\) or \(2x-1<-7\). First, \(2x-1>7\) gives \(2x>8\), so \(x>4\). Second, \(2x-1<-7\) gives \(2x<-6\), so \(x<-3\). Therefore the solution is \(x<-3\) or \(x>4\). The option \(-3<x<4\) is the solution of \(|2x-1|<7\), not \(|2x-1|>7\).

questions.concept: Comparing two absolute values with an inequality
questions.learningObjective: Solve an inequality of the form \(|x-a|\ge |x-b|\) by squaring both sides.
questions.question: Solve \(|x-1|\ge |x+3|\).
questions.explanation:
Since both sides are nonnegative, square both sides:
\[
(x-1)^2\ge (x+3)^2
\]
Expand: \(x^2-2x+1\ge x^2+6x+9\). Subtract \(x^2\) from both sides: \(-2x+1\ge 6x+9\). Then \(-8x\ge 8\), so \(x\le -1\). Therefore the solution is \(x\le -1\). For example, \(x=-2\) satisfies the original inequality, while \(x=0\) does not.
questions.hint: Because both absolute values are nonnegative, squaring both sides preserves the inequality direction.

questions.concept: Solving strict inequalities involving two absolute values
questions.question: Solve \(|2x+1|<|x-2|\).
questions.explanation:
Square both sides:
\[
(2x+1)^2<(x-2)^2
\]
Expand: \(4x^2+4x+1<x^2-4x+4\). Bring all terms to one side: \(3x^2+8x-3<0\). Factor: \((3x-1)(x+3)<0\). The critical values are \(x=-3\) and \(x=\frac{1}{3}\). Since the quadratic opens upward, it is negative between the roots. Therefore the solution is \(-3<x<\frac{1}{3}\). The option \(x<-3\) or \(x>\frac{1}{3}\) corresponds to the reversed inequality.
questions.hint: After squaring, move all terms to one side and factor the resulting quadratic.

questions.concept: Parameter conditions for absolute value inequalities
questions.learningObjective: Determine a parameter value that makes an absolute value inequality have exactly one solution.
questions.question: For what value of \(k\) does the inequality \(|2x-1|\le k\) have exactly one solution?
questions.explanation: The inequality \(|2x-1|\le k\) has exactly one solution when the right side is \(0\), because then \(|2x-1|\le 0\) forces \(2x-1=0\). This gives \(x=\frac{1}{2}\), exactly one solution. If \(k=2\), then \(-2\le 2x-1\le 2\), which gives infinitely many solutions. Therefore \(k=0\).
questions.hint: Compare the solution sets of \(|u|\le k\) for \(k>0\), \(k=0\), and \(k<0\).
